lessons.title: Listen and speak: what are you doing?
lessons.course:
To say what someone is doing now, we use is + verb + ing.
She is washing her hands. He is brushing his teeth. They are sweeping the compound.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
She is washing her hands.
He is brushing his teeth.

lessons.model: The adult mimes washing hands and asks: “What am I doing?” Then answers: “I am washing my hands.”
lessons.guided: Mime healthy actions (washing hands, brushing teeth, drinking clean water). The other person says what you are doing.
lessons.exercise: Look: Ekane has a toothbrush in his mouth. What is he doing?
lessons.remediation: Use only “I am …ing” while doing the action yourself.
lessons.transfer: Say what each person at home is doing at this moment.
lessons.materials: Soap, a towel, a toothbrush (or pictures of them).

practice.prompt: Listen and say after the voice.
practice.listen: She is washing her hands with soap.
practice.answer: She is washing her hands with soap.
practice.explanation: We use is + ing for actions now.

practice.prompt: Complete with the right action.
practice.text: He is [[brushing]] his teeth. She is [[drinking]] clean water.
practice.explanation: The verb ends with ing.

practice.prompt: Which sentence tells what is happening now?
practice.explanation: is + ing shows an action happening now.

lessons.title: Read: looking at pictures, answering questions
lessons.objective: Interpret a picture and read a very short text silently, then answer questions.
lessons.course:
A picture tells a story. We look at who is in the picture, where they are and what they are doing.
Then we read the short text and answer the questions with words from the text.

support.title: Read silently
support.text: Enow is sick. He is in bed. His mother gives him water. The nurse comes to see him.

lessons.model: The adult looks at a picture of a clinic and says: “I see a nurse. She has a thermometer. A child is sitting on a bed.”
lessons.guided: Read the short text silently. Then answer: Who is sick? Where is he? Who comes to see him?
lessons.exercise: Read the text. Who comes to see Enow?
accept: The nurse comes to see him
lessons.remediation: Read the text aloud with the adult first, then answer one question at a time.
lessons.transfer: Look at a picture in a book at home and say three things you see.
lessons.materials: A picture of a clinic or a sick child (drawing).

practice.prompt: “Enow is sick. He is in bed.” Where is Enow?
practice.explanation: The text says: He is in bed.

practice.prompt: Who gives Enow water?
practice.explanation: The text says: His mother gives him water.

practice.prompt: Put the sentences in the order of the text.
items: The nurse comes to see him.
practice.answer: Enow is sick. He is in bed. His mother gives him water. The nurse comes to see him.
practice.explanation: Follow the order of the story.

lessons.title: Build words with jumbled letters
lessons.objective: Put jumbled letters in order to build words about health.
lessons.course:
Sometimes the letters of a word are mixed up. We say the sounds and try different orders until we find a real word.
p-a-s-o gives soap. d-e-b gives bed.

support.title: Build with the adult
support.text:
o s a p → soap
d e b → bed

lessons.model: The adult mixes the cards b, e, d and says: “Which sound comes first? b… e… d: bed!”
lessons.guided: Use letter cards. Build the word, read it, then write it.
lessons.exercise: Build the word with the letters: n, d, a, h (we wash it).
lessons.remediation: Give the first letter of the word, then build the rest.
lessons.transfer: Mix the letters of your name and ask someone to build it again.

practice.prompt: Put the letters in order to build “soap”.
practice.explanation: We wash with soap.

practice.prompt: Build the word: t-e-e-h-t (we brush them).
practice.explanation: We brush our teeth.

practice.prompt: Write the word you built: soap.
practice.explanation: s-o-a-p.

lessons.title: Describing words and opposites
lessons.objective: Use common adjectives and their opposites: clean/dirty, big/small, hot/cold, sick/well.
lessons.course:
An adjective describes a noun. Clean hands. A big bottle. Hot tea.
Many adjectives have an opposite: clean – dirty, big – small, hot – cold, sick – well.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
clean ↔ dirty
big ↔ small
hot ↔ cold

lessons.model: The adult shows two cloths: “This cloth is clean. This cloth is dirty.” Then two cups: “This cup is big. This one is small.”
lessons.guided: Sort picture pairs: say the adjective for each picture and its opposite.
lessons.remediation: Work with real objects (two cups, two cloths) and one pair of opposites at a time.
lessons.transfer: Find something big and something small in your kitchen.
lessons.materials: Pairs of objects: two cups, two cloths, warm and cool water.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its opposite.
practice.explanation: Opposites mean the contrary.

practice.prompt: Complete with an adjective.
practice.explanation: We wash our hands to keep them clean.

practice.prompt: Which word describes the water? “The water is ___.”
practice.explanation: Cold is an adjective: it describes the water.

lessons.title: Halves and quarters
lessons.objective: Share a whole into 2 or 4 equal parts and name a half and a quarter.
lessons.course:
When we cut a whole into 2 equal parts, each part is a half (½).
When we cut it into 4 equal parts, each part is a quarter (¼).
The parts must be equal.
lessons.model: The adult cuts a pawpaw into 2 equal parts: “Each part is a half.” Then cuts each half again: “Now there are 4 quarters.”
lessons.guided: Fold a sheet of paper in 2 equal parts, then in 4. Colour a half, then a quarter.
lessons.exercise: A mango is cut into 2 equal parts. What is each part called?
lessons.remediation: Fold paper in two and check that the two parts are the same.
lessons.transfer: Share a fruit equally with a brother or a sister.
lessons.materials: Paper sheets, a fruit, a knife (used by the adult only).

practice.prompt: How many quarters make a whole?
practice.explanation: 4 quarters make one whole.

practice.prompt: Which picture shows a half? A cake cut into …
practice.explanation: A half is one of 2 equal parts.

practice.prompt: Match each sharing with its name.
practice.explanation: The number of equal parts gives the name.

lessons.title: Sharing equally
lessons.objective: Share items objectively into equal groups and check that each group has the same number.
lessons.course: To share equally, each person gets the same number. 12 oranges for 3 children: we give one at a time to each child until there are none left. Each child gets 4.
lessons.model: The adult shares 10 tablets of soap between 2 families: “One for you, one for you… Each family gets 5.”
lessons.guided: Share stones between 2, then 3, then 4 people, one at a time. Check the groups are equal.
lessons.exercise: Share 8 bananas equally between 2 children. How many does each child get?
lessons.remediation: Share between 2 people only, with even numbers.
lessons.transfer: Help to share food equally at home.

practice.prompt: Share 6 sweets equally between 3 children. How many each?
practice.explanation: 6 shared by 3: 2 each.

practice.prompt: Share 15 pencils between 5 pupils. How many each?
practice.explanation: Give one at a time: 3 each.

practice.prompt: Is this fair? Bih gets 4 mangoes, Tabi gets 2 mangoes.
practice.explanation: Fair sharing gives the same number to each.

lessons.title: Adding the same number: the table of 2
lessons.objective: Build the multiplication table of 2 by adding 2 again and again.
lessons.course:
When we add the same number many times, we multiply. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6, so 3 times 2 is 6: 3 × 2 = 6.
Table of 2: 1 × 2 = 2, 2 × 2 = 4, 3 × 2 = 6, 4 × 2 = 8, 5 × 2 = 10.
lessons.model: The adult counts the eyes of children: “1 child: 2 eyes. 2 children: 4 eyes. 3 children: 6 eyes. 3 × 2 = 6.”
lessons.guided: Make groups of 2 stones. Add a group each time and say the table.
lessons.remediation: Count in 2s with pairs of objects before writing ×.
lessons.transfer: Count the legs of the chickens at home with the table of 2.

practice.prompt: Complete the table of 2.
practice.explanation: Add 2 each time.

practice.prompt: 3 children each wash 2 hands. How many hands?

lessons.title: A picture graph of healthy food
lessons.objective: Represent data with a picture graph and read it.
lessons.course:
A picture graph uses pictures to show how many. Each picture stands for one thing.
The longest row shows the most. The shortest row shows the least.
lessons.model: The adult asks the family their favourite fruit and puts one fruit drawing per person in rows: banana, orange, mango.
lessons.guided: Ask five people their favourite healthy food. Draw one picture per answer in the right row. Say which row is the longest.
lessons.exercise: In a picture graph: bananas ●●●, oranges ●●●●●, mangoes ●●. Which fruit is liked most?
lessons.remediation: Make a graph with real objects in rows before drawing it.
lessons.transfer: Make a picture graph of the fruits eaten at home this week.
lessons.materials: Paper, coloured pencils or small fruit drawings.

practice.prompt: Bananas ●●●, oranges ●●●●●, mangoes ●●. How many people like mangoes?
practice.explanation: There are 2 pictures for mangoes.

practice.prompt: Which fruit is liked least?
practice.explanation: The mango row is the shortest.

practice.prompt: How many more people like oranges than bananas?

lessons.title: Malaria and the mosquito net
lessons.objective: Name common diseases of the locality, say how malaria is caught and why we sleep under a mosquito net.
lessons.course:
Some common diseases are malaria, cough and diarrhoea.
Malaria comes from the bite of a mosquito. To avoid it, we sleep under a mosquito net every night and we remove dirty water around the house.
Good habits also protect us: wash hands before eating, drink clean water, eat fruits.
lessons.model: Every night, Manka’s mother tucks the mosquito net under the mattress so that mosquitoes cannot enter.
lessons.guided: Look at a mosquito net. Practise tucking it under a mattress or a mat. Say: “I sleep under a mosquito net.”
lessons.remediation: Use a picture of a mosquito and a net; repeat one sentence: “The net stops the mosquito.”
lessons.transfer: Check tonight that your mosquito net has no holes.
lessons.materials: A mosquito net or a picture of one.

practice.prompt: Where do we sleep to avoid malaria?
practice.explanation: The net stops mosquitoes.

practice.prompt: Match each good habit with what it prevents.
practice.answer: net: malaria; washing hands: diarrhoea; clean water: stomach ache.
practice.explanation: Good habits keep diseases away.

practice.prompt: Say one thing we do around the house to have fewer mosquitoes.
practice.answer: Remove dirty water, empty old tins and bottles.
practice.explanation: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water.

lessons.title: J’aime, je n’aime pas
lessons.objective: Dire ce qu’on aime et ce qu’on n’aime pas, et réagir à des instructions simples.
lessons.course:
Pour dire ses goûts : « J’aime les mangues. » (I like mangoes.) « Je n’aime pas le bruit. » (I do not like noise.)
Des instructions simples : « Lève-toi. » (Stand up.) « Assieds-toi. » (Sit down.) « Lave-toi les mains. » (Wash your hands.) « Bois de l’eau. » (Drink some water.)

support.title: Dis avec l’adulte
support.text:
J’aime les fruits.
Je n’aime pas être malade.
Lave-toi les mains !

lessons.model: L’adulte dit : « Lève-toi ! » et Bih se lève. « Lave-toi les mains ! » et Bih mime le lavage des mains. Puis elle dit : « J’aime les oranges. »
lessons.guided: Jeu « Jacques a dit » en français : l’adulte donne une instruction, l’enfant l’exécute. Puis l’enfant dit un aliment qu’il aime.
lessons.exercise: Dis un fruit que tu aimes en français.
lessons.remediation: Commence par « J’aime … » avec des images de fruits.
lessons.transfer: Au repas, dis en français ce que tu aimes.

practice.prompt: Relie l’instruction à son geste.
practice.answer: Lève-toi : stand up ; Assieds-toi : sit down ; Lave-toi les mains : wash your hands.
practice.explanation: Chaque instruction demande un geste.

practice.prompt: Complète.
practice.explanation: « J’aime » veut dire I like.

practice.prompt: Écoute et fais le geste.
practice.explanation: Écoute bien avant de bouger.

lessons.title: My rights and my duties
lessons.objective: Identify some rights of the child (education, identity, health) and the duties that go with them.
lessons.course:
Every child has rights: a name and a birth certificate (identity), to go to school (education), to be cared for when sick (health), to play and to be protected.
We also have duties: to respect others, to work at school, to help at home.
lessons.model: Enow is sick. His parents take him to the health centre: he has the right to health. When he is well, he does his homework: it is his duty.
lessons.guided: Sort picture cards: a right or a duty. Explain one of each.
lessons.exercise: Name one right of the child.
lessons.answer: For example: to go to school.
lessons.remediation: Start with two rights the child knows: going to school and having a name.
lessons.transfer: Ask your parents where your birth certificate is kept.
lessons.materials: Picture cards of rights and duties.

practice.prompt: Match each right with what it gives.
pairs: a name and a birth certificate
practice.answer: education: school; health: care; identity: name.
practice.explanation: Rights protect children.

practice.prompt: Which one is a duty?
practice.explanation: Respecting others is something we must do: a duty.

practice.prompt: Say one duty you have at home.
practice.answer: For example: help to clean the house.
practice.explanation: Duties are things we do to help others.

lessons.title: Our little garden: watering and weeding
lessons.objective: Use simple garden tools safely and care for plants by watering and weeding.
lessons.course:
In a garden we grow vegetables: tomatoes, okra, green beans, huckleberry (njama njama).
We care for plants: we water them in the morning or the evening, we pull out the weeds, we use manure to feed the soil.
We use small tools carefully and we wear shoes in the garden.
lessons.model: Every evening, Enow waters the okra plants with a watering can. On Saturday he pulls out the weeds.
lessons.guided: Plant a seed in a tin or a corner of the yard. Water it and watch it grow each day.
lessons.answer: In the morning or in the evening.
accept: in the morning or in the evening
In the morning or in the evening
lessons.remediation: Water one plant every day with the adult and look at it.
lessons.transfer: Keep your plant alive for two weeks and tell the class how it grew.
lessons.materials: Seeds, a tin with soil, water, a small watering can.

practice.prompt: Match each tool with its use.
practice.answer: watering can: water; hoe: dig; manure: feed the soil.
practice.explanation: Each thing helps the garden.

practice.prompt: What are weeds?
choices: plants we did not plant that we pull out
practice.answer: plants we did not plant that we pull out
practice.explanation: Weeds take water and food from our plants.

practice.prompt: Put in order how a plant grows.
practice.answer: seed, small plant, big plant, fruit.
practice.explanation: A plant grows step by step.

lessons.title: A poster: wash your hands
lessons.objective: Draw and colour a simple poster to give a health message.
lessons.course:
A poster gives a message with a drawing and a few words. It must be clear and easy to see from far: big drawing, bright colours, few words.
Our message: “Wash your hands.”
lessons.model: The adult draws two big hands under a tap with soap bubbles and writes: “Wash your hands.”
lessons.guided: Draw a big picture of hands being washed. Colour it with bright colours. Copy the message with the adult.
lessons.exercise: What does a poster need to be seen from far?
lessons.answer: A big drawing and bright colours.
accept: A big drawing and bright colours
lessons.remediation: Draw the hands first, then add the tap and the soap.
lessons.transfer: Put your poster near the place where your family washes hands.
lessons.materials: Large paper, coloured pencils or paint.

practice.prompt: Draw your poster.
practice.answer: A poster with hands, soap and water.
practice.explanation: Make the drawing big and clear.

practice.prompt: Which poster is easier to read from far?
practice.explanation: Big and simple is easier to see.

practice.prompt: Write the message of your poster.
practice.explanation: Copy the words carefully.

lessons.title: Keep-fit exercises for a healthy body
lessons.objective: Perform simple keep-fit exercises to stay healthy.
lessons.course:
Exercise keeps the body strong and healthy. Simple exercises: arm circles, jumping jacks, touching the toes, running on the spot.
We breathe well, we drink water and we stop if we feel pain.
lessons.model: The adult counts: “Arm circles, 1 to 10. Jumping jacks, 1 to 10. Touch your toes, 1 to 10.”
lessons.guided: Do each exercise ten times while counting aloud. Then rest and breathe slowly.
lessons.answer: For example: jumping jacks or arm circles.
lessons.remediation: Do each exercise five times only.
lessons.transfer: Do your keep-fit exercises every morning for a week.

practice.prompt: Do 10 jumping jacks and 10 arm circles. How many movements in all?
What do we do if we feel pain?
choices: we stop and tell an adult
practice.answer: we stop and tell an adult
practice.explanation: Pain is a signal to stop.

practice.prompt: Why do we exercise?
practice.answer: To keep the body strong and healthy.
practice.explanation: Exercise is good for the heart and the muscles.

lessons.title: Traditional meals of my family
lessons.objective: Use appropriate words to describe a traditional meal of the locality.
lessons.course:
Every region has traditional meals: achu and yellow soup, ndolé, eru, koki, kwacoco, fufu and njama njama, mbongo tchobi, and many more. Many are made with local vegetables that are good for health.
We name the meal and its ingredients in our language.
lessons.model: Manka’s mother prepares eru with waterleaf. Manka learns the names of the vegetables in her mother’s language.
lessons.guided: Ask the adult the name of a family meal and two ingredients in the family language.
lessons.exercise: Name a traditional meal of your family.
lessons.answer: The child names a traditional meal.
lessons.remediation: Look at one meal on the table and name it.
lessons.transfer: Help to prepare a simple traditional meal with an adult.
lessons.materials: Pictures of meals or real ingredients.

practice.prompt: Which traditional meals are made with green leaves?
practice.explanation: Ndolé and eru are made with leaves.

practice.prompt: Say the name of a vegetable in your family language.
practice.answer: A vegetable name in the family language.
practice.explanation: Ask an adult to help you.

practice.prompt: Draw your favourite traditional meal.
practice.explanation: Show the ingredients.

lessons.title: Screens and my health
lessons.objective: Use screens safely: not too long, not too close, and with an adult.
lessons.course:
Screens are useful but we use them wisely. We sit far from the television, we do not watch for a long time, we stop before sleeping and we rest our eyes. We do not touch a device with wet hands.
Playing outside and sleeping well are good for health.
lessons.model: After watching a cartoon, Tabi turns off the television and goes to play outside.
lessons.guided: Make a family rule for screens: how long, where to sit, when to stop. Draw it.
lessons.exercise: Do we sit close to or far from the television?
lessons.remediation: Practise one rule: turn off the screen when the adult says so.
lessons.transfer: Follow your family screen rule for a week.

practice.prompt: Which one is a good screen habit?
practice.explanation: We need good sleep.

practice.prompt: Is it safe to touch a phone with wet hands? Answer yes or no.
practice.explanation: Water and electricity are dangerous together.

practice.prompt: Say one thing you can do instead of watching a screen.
practice.answer: For example: play outside, read, draw.
practice.explanation: Other activities are good for health.
